title: Slack MCP — Channels, Threads & Messages in Claude Code

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

Lesson 2-12 introduced Slack AI — the native AI features built into the Slack app. This lesson goes further: you'll connect Slack to Claude Code via MCP, enabling multi-tool workflows, bulk channel analysis, and cross-platform synthesis that Slack AI alone cannot do.

## What Slack MCP Can Do

Slack has an official MCP server maintained by Slack (part of Salesforce). It is one of the most capable and stable MCP servers available.

**Reading:**
- List all workspaces, channels, and direct messages
- Read message history from any channel or DM
- Retrieve thread replies
- Search messages across your entire Slack workspace with natural language

**Writing:**
- Post messages to any channel
- Reply to threads
- Create new channels (if you have permission)

**People:**
- Look up users and their profiles
- List members of a channel

**Combined with other MCPs:** Slack is often the real-time pulse of a team. Combining Slack MCP with email, calendar, or Notion MCPs lets you answer questions like: *"Based on my Slack channels and my calendar, what projects am I currently the most blocked on?"*

## Setup — Slack MCP

**Step 1 — Create a Slack app**

1. Go to api.slack.com/apps → **Create New App** → **From scratch**
2. App name: `claude-mcp` → select your workspace → **Create App**
3. In the left sidebar, go to **OAuth & Permissions**
4. Scroll to **Scopes** → **Bot Token Scopes** → Add scopes:
   - `channels:read` — list public channels
   - `channels:history` — read public channel messages
   - `groups:read` and `groups:history` — same for private channels
   - `im:read` and `im:history` — direct messages
   - `mpim:read` and `mpim:history` — group DMs
   - `search:read` — search messages
   - `chat:write` — post messages
   - `users:read` — look up user profiles
5. Scroll up to **OAuth Tokens** → **Install to Workspace** → Authorize
6. Copy the **Bot User OAuth Token** (starts with `xoxb-`) — save it

**Step 2 — Install the server**

Slack provides an official MCP server. Check github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers for the official Slack server, or:
```
npm install -g @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack
```

**Step 3 — Configure Claude Code**

In `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`:
```json
"slack": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack"],
  "env": {
    "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "xoxb-your-token-here",
    "SLACK_TEAM_ID": "your-workspace-team-id"
  }
}
```
Find your Team ID: in Slack web, go to your workspace URL — the ID starts with `T` in the URL path (e.g., `T01ABC123`). Save and relaunch Claude Code.

**Step 4 — Verify**
```
launch claude → /mcp → confirm slack is listed
Ask: "List the 5 most active channels in my Slack workspace."
```

**Bot vs. user token:** This setup uses a Bot token, meaning Claude Code reads and posts as your app bot (not as you personally). Messages posted by Claude will appear as coming from `claude-mcp` bot. If your workspace restricts bot posting, you may need a User token instead — check api.slack.com/authentication/token-types for the difference and ask your Slack admin.

sections.title: Slack Intelligence Across Your Workspace
sections.content:
With Slack MCP connected, run these tasks. Each builds on the previous.

**Task 1 — Workspace overview**
```
Ask: "List all the channels I have access to in my Slack workspace.
Group them by likely purpose: team channels, project channels, general channels."
```

**Task 2 — Catch up on a busy channel**
```
Ask: "Read the last 48 hours of messages in #[your-busiest-channel].
Summarize: what was discussed, what decisions were made, and what
anyone is waiting on."
```

**Task 3 — Find a piece of information**
Think of something you remember was discussed in Slack but would take time to find manually:
```
Ask: "Search Slack for any messages about [topic]. Find the most relevant
discussion and tell me: when it was, who was involved, and what the outcome was."
```

**Task 4 — Identify action items you've been tagged in**
```
Ask: "Search my Slack messages for any place where someone mentioned
my name or @mentioned me in the last week and was asking me to do
something or waiting for a response from me. List each one with the
channel, sender, and what they need."
```
This is the Slack equivalent of the Outlook inbox-triage task from lesson 8-16.

**Task 5 — Draft and post a message (optional)**
```
Ask: "Draft a message to post in #[channel] announcing that [thing].
Keep it concise, friendly, and under 3 sentences. Then post it."
```
Review the draft before confirming. Claude will ask for confirmation before posting.

**Record in your notes:** Which task produced the most useful result for you personally?

sections.question: Your Slack MCP bot token has `channels:history` scope but not `groups:history`. When you ask Claude Code to summarize a private channel, what will happen?
options: Claude will summarize the private channel because private channels are just channels
Claude will get an error or empty result because private channels require the groups:history scope
Claude will ask you to make the channel public first
Claude will use a different authentication method automatically
sections.explanation: Slack's API treats public channels and private channels (groups) as separate resources with separate permission scopes. channels:history covers public channels; groups:history covers private channels. Without the correct scope, the API returns a permissions error or empty results — Claude cannot work around this. The fix is to go back to your Slack app settings, add the groups:history scope, reinstall the app to your workspace, and get a new token.

sections.content: **You've completed lesson 8-18.** Slack is now connected to Claude Code. You can search your entire workspace history, get channel summaries, find action items addressed to you, and post messages — all from the terminal.
